description: Agent selects between two stress analysis methods for a composite laminate panel. No hard trigger applies, but the choice has moderate materiality warranting disclosure to the user.

input.description: Choosing Classical Laminate Theory (CLT) over finite element analysis for predicting interlaminar stresses in a carbon fiber reinforced polymer panel under bending load
input.context: Structural analysis of a CFRP panel (8-ply quasi-isotropic layup) for a preliminary design check. The panel thickness-to-span ratio is 1:15, which is near the boundary where CLT assumptions begin to lose accuracy.

candidate.question: Should Classical Laminate Theory or a 3D finite element model be used to predict interlaminar stresses in this composite panel?
candidate.reason: The panel's thickness-to-span ratio of 1:15 is near the boundary where CLT's plane-stress assumption becomes inaccurate for interlaminar stress predictions. CLT may underestimate through-thickness stresses by 15-30% in this regime.

alternatives.label: Classical Laminate Theory
alternatives.description: Use CLT with Tsai-Wu failure criterion to evaluate in-plane and estimated interlaminar stresses.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Computationally fast and well-understood. Assumes plane stress and may underestimate through-thickness stresses for panels near the thick-plate threshold.

alternatives.label: 3D finite element model
alternatives.description: Use a solid-element FE model with at least two elements through each ply thickness to resolve interlaminar stress gradients.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Captures three-dimensional stress states accurately. Requires significantly more computational resources and careful mesh convergence study. May be excessive for a preliminary design check.

candidate.uncertainty: The accuracy boundary for CLT at this thickness-to-span ratio has not been validated against test data for this specific layup sequence.
